panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: ±10.7% implied is roughly fair, not cheap: mean abs of last 8 prints is 9.69% and of the last 4 is ~9.1%. I expect a realised move at or slightly inside implied, with a fatter left tail.
key_drivers: The bar sits above management's own guide: 39-week adj EPS is $1.95 vs FY26 guide $2.40-2.60, so guidance implies Q4 adj EPS mid $0.55 while consensus is $0.62 -- the Street needs a top-of-range print just to be in line.

The metric that actually trades: initial FY2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance plus the promised 'return to sales growth'. A FY27 midpoint of $740M+ holds the stock; anything with a 7.2-7.3 handle reads as a walk-down. UNFI's habit is a wide, low-midpoint initial guide.

Profitability recovery is genuine and the comp is soft (Q3 adj EBITDA +16.6% to $183M against a cyber-depressed Q4 FY25 base), but revenue has missed two quarters running, which is precisely what cost the stock -10.3% in June.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The YoY optics are almost rigged to look great off the cyber-depressed Q4 FY25 base, and if the FY27 guide shows the network-optimization sales drag annualising out into growth, the revenue-miss narrative dies and the stock re-rates on a 13x forward multiple -- the exact +18.45% template from the September 2025 print.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source a dated 30/60/90-day revision series or an explicit FY27 EBITDA consensus dollar figure; the FY27 anchor is snippet_only.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Event-implied ±10.7% is essentially the historical median and above the last four prints (mean abs 9.09%) -- fairly priced, not rich, not cheap. But the two prior Q4/initial-FY-guidance prints were +30.56% and +18.45%, the two largest in the sample, so I treat 10.7% as a 1SD with a fatter right tail than the straddle prices.
key_drivers: Positioning is de-risked, not crowded: stock is -23.5% from its 52-week high set the day before the last print; short interest only 4.44% of float, 5.4 days to cover -- no squeeze fuel either way, the crowded-turnaround-long has already been shaken out.

Front-expiry options tilt upside and skew is inverted: Sep-18 call OI outweighs put OI roughly 2:1, and call IV exceeds put IV at every strike -- persistent right-tail demand, though aggregate all-expiry OI is put-heavy (likely longer-dated protection/collars).
The contrarian offset: a new CFO's first print sets initial FY2027 guidance. New CFOs sandbag opening bars -- the mechanism that reproduces June's beat-but-fall (-10.28% despite an EPS beat).
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: Initial FY2027 sales guidance embeds another leg of network-optimization shrinkage and a new CFO lowballs the EBITDA bar on his first call -- exactly the setup that took the stock down 10.3% in June on numbers that read fine.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: No borrow fee, dealer gamma, or live options-flow data reachable; short interest is ~3 weeks stale, pre-dating the last leg of the drawdown.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: I expect ~11-14% absolute, slightly larger than the ±10.7% implied. This is UNFI's fiscal-Q4 print, which carries initial full-year guidance, and both prior Q4 prints in the sample sit at the fat end of the distribution.
key_drivers: Positioning is de-crowded, not crowded: hype peaked at the 52-week high the day before the last print; the stock has bled three months, sits below both the 50- and 200-day averages -- neither bulls nor bears trapped, the pain trade leans mildly up.

The demand signal is real and separable from social noise: Whole Foods (~22% of revenue) extended primary distribution through 2032 and is actively adding units. No meme/pump fingerprints found; StockTwits sentiment/message-volume metrics returned N/A.

Narrative fragility sits in the guide, not the quarter: the bull story requires a 'return to growth' FY27 guide from a CFO four weeks in the seat plus a broader leadership reshuffle -- the textbook conservative-first-guide setup.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: A conservative or reset FY27 guide from the new CFO breaks the 'return to growth' story the crowd is holding -- this tape has already shown it sells strength (gapped down intraday, closed up, then fully reversed the next session).
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: No live social series sourced; the 7/14/30-day tone-change read is inferred from price versus moving averages, not measured social data.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Base rate says ±10-13% absolute. Anchor set: mean abs 9.69%, median abs 10.23%, and exactly 4 of 8 prints exceeded 10.7% -- the implied sits right on the median, if anything marginally cheap for this specific Q4/initial-guidance print.
key_drivers: Directional base rate is near a coin flip: 5 up / 3 down over the 8 anchor prints, but the last 3 are 1 up / 2 down; extending to earlier sourced quarters pulls the long-run split toward roughly 50/50 -- effective sample is thin.

Mechanism repeats regardless of story: the last two prints both paired an EPS beat/in-line with a revenue miss and both fell. The intentional network-optimization revenue drag does not anniversary until Q1 FY27, so the same top-line optics are structurally likely again.
Setup offsets: the run-in is de-risked, down roughly 10% from its mid-August high, which historically lowers the bar; a brand-new CFO delivering the first FY27 guide is a conservative-reset cohort.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The two most recent Q4/September prints were +18.45% and +30.56% -- this is the one quarter of UNFI's year that has repeatedly gapped violently higher on a conservative-then-credible FY guide into a beaten-down float, a live large-magnitude counter-base-rate that the implied ±10.7% underprices.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source exact close-to-close percentages for the 2022/2023 Q4 prints (direction confirmed negative, magnitude unsourced); MarketChameleon and stockanalysis earnings tables returned access-denied.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: ±10.7% implied is roughly fair, maybe 0.5-1pt rich against mean abs 9.69% / median 10.23%. Own centre of gravity is a -4% to -8% drift-lower outcome with a real 30-35% chance of a >+10% squeeze. Macro contributes maybe 1-2pts of the move, not 10.
key_drivers: Peer split cuts both ways: the distribution cohort (Sysco, US Foods, Performance Food Group) worked on margin/cost-out, while UNFI's actual demand base -- grocery retail (Albertsons, Sprouts, Natural Grocers) -- is soft on volume this season.

Regime is hostile to levered small-cap value into the print: August payrolls beat sharply, 10y yield ~4.8% (highest since Nov 2023), ~54% September-hike odds, Russell 2000 fell 1.4% on 9/4 while the S&P was flat.

This market has already punished UNFI for 'maintained not raised': on 6/9/26 the stock fell ~10.3% despite adj EBITDA +16.6% because sales missed and guidance was only narrowed; sell-side average PT (~$45-49) leaves little target-gap fuel.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: An initial FY27 adjusted EBITDA guide materially above the ~$695M FY26 midpoint would swamp every macro and peer input and squeeze a de-risked small cap violently higher, exactly as the March 2026 EPS guide raise did.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source current short interest/borrow cost or confirm any S&P rebalance exposure; several peer one-day reactions are snippet-sourced rather than fetched.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: I expect realised move of roughly ±12-16%, at or above the ±10.7% anchor. The raw straddle-to-spot of ~13.6% is probably closer to the truth than the term-structure-adjusted figure, given the scale of the information event. I would not sell this straddle.
key_drivers: First FY2027 guide from a CFO four weeks in the seat; the company has only ever given a 'framework' off the $695M FY26 baseline, never a hard FY27 number -- the $730M+ figures in circulation are analyst constructions, not guidance.
$40M of FY26-YTD cyber-insurance proceeds against $22M of cyber costs sits in the base and does not repeat in FY27 -- the FY27 bridge starts in a hole.

June 2026 precedent is directly on tape: profit beat + revenue miss + no raise = ~16% premarket drop; Q4 revenue is guided down again and the network-optimization drag is not fully lapped until Q1 FY27.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The -14% slide into the print with zero company-specific news may already BE the de-risking; a merely in-line FY27 guide plus confirmed sub-2x leverage could produce a +15-20% squeeze -- a move size that appears three times in the last eight prints.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source short interest, float short %, or borrow cost; no formal FY2027 sell-side EBITDA consensus obtainable, and cyber-insurance treatment in the adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation was not retrievable.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: ±10.7% implied is fairly priced to slightly cheap versus an 8-print mean abs of 9.7% and median 10.2%; the distribution is fat-tailed on both sides. My skew is toward the downside tail, but the size of the move is priced -- the direction is not.
key_drivers: No insider buying since January; two discretionary (non-10b5-1) officer sales near the highs in May/June, then silence, against zero buying into a 15% drawdown -- the only 2026 buy (a director, ~$573k) is eight months stale and was not added-to on the way down.

Five C-suite changes in seven weeks ahead of the print that introduces FY27 guidance, with the new CFO in seat under a month -- rebasing risk on the guide, not on the quarter. A Chief Corporate Affairs Officer exit was disclosed only via a transaction-free Form 4, with no 8-K.

The Q3 call already hedged: fuel cost pressure and incremental technology investment were explicitly loaded into Q4, working-capital benefits flagged as not repeating at the same magnitude, and guidance was narrowed with midpoints held (neutral) -- no pre-announcement either way.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: UNFI habitually beats EPS (~30% average trailing surprise) and the balance sheet story is real (net debt lowest since FY2018). If the new CFO simply ratifies the three-year algorithm rather than rebasing it, a $43 stock with this move history squeezes 15-20% and my forensic read is right about the turnover and wrong about the tape.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source current short interest, borrow fee, or options positioning; Item 5 of the Q3 10-Q was too large to parse so 10b5-1 adoption/termination disclosures are unverified.

synthesis.move_band_note: unsigned magnitude band, right-skewed; the implied move is roughly one standard deviation, not a cap
synthesis.early_prediction: Panel is tightly aligned near zero (consensus -4.4, disparity 26.5) -- genuinely no directional edge, not a split masked by a headline. The wider signal is asymmetric reversal risk: reversal_risk maxes at 72 (red-team), driven by a first FY2027 EBITDA guide from a CFO four weeks in the seat, against a live counter-base-rate that UNFI's last two Q4/initial-guide prints were the two largest moves in the sample (+30.56%, +18.45%). Direction is a coin flip; whichever way it breaks, it likely breaks big.
synthesis.red_team_survival_note: The red-team case (-12, but reversal_risk 72, the panel ceiling) rests on a specific, sourced mechanism -- a brand-new CFO's first FY27 guide, a non-repeating $40M cyber-insurance cushion in the FY26 base, and a directly analogous June 2026 precedent (beat + narrowed guide = -10.3%). It does not go unanswered: two personas (options-positioning +16, sentiment +12) independently read the same new-CFO fact as a de-risked/sandbagged-bar setup favoring upside rather than pure downside risk, from different evidence (options skew/positioning vs technical de-risking and the Whole Foods demand signal). That is a genuine disagreement about which way a single known catalyst cuts, not a case going unanswered -- consistent with the aligned-but-modest-certainty read rather than a Lean Down.
